evidence.quote: In light of these uncertainties, the Committee decided to await more evidence that the recovery’s progress will be sustained before adjusting the pace of asset purchases.
Thus, the first increases in short-term rates might not occur until the unemployment rate is considerably below 6½ percent.
However, the tightening of financial conditions observed in recent months, if sustained, could slow the pace of improvement in the economy and the labor market.
The Committee recognizes that inflation persistently below its objective could pose risks to economic performance, and we will continue to monitor inflation developments closely.
Notably, at 7.3 percent, the unemployment rate remains well above acceptable levels.
So this was a step—it was a step, a precautionary step if you will.

parsed.rationale: The Chair explains the surprise decision not to taper. He cites insufficient data confirmation, tighter financial conditions, fiscal risks and below-target inflation, and stresses patient, highly accommodative rate guidance, while still holding open a possible taper later in the year.
